## Overview

This assignment loads the same book dataset from two hand-generated files — an HTML table (`books.html`) and a JSON array (`books.json`) — into separate R data frames and then verifies that the two frames are identical after normalizing data types.

The dataset covers three graphic novels in the *Teen Titans* series by Kami Garcia and Gabriel Picolo (DC Comics), with ISBN, publication year, and publisher as additional attributes.

## Approach

## Challenges

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1 · Load the HTML data

```{r load-html}
library(rvest)

df_html <- read_html("books.html") |>
  html_table() |>
  _[[1]]           # html_table() returns a list; grab the first (only) table

# Trim any stray whitespace that the HTML parser may have captured
df_html <- as.data.frame(lapply(df_html, trimws))

# Inspect
str(df_html)
df_html
```

> **Note on types:** `html_table()` reads every cell as a character string, so `pub_year` arrives as `"2023"`, `"2024"`, `"2026"` — not integers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2 · Load the JSON data

```{r load-json}
library(jsonlite)

df_json <- fromJSON("books.json")

# Inspect
str(df_json)
df_json
```

> **Note on types:** `fromJSON()` auto-detects JSON types, so `pub_year` (stored as a bare integer in the JSON) arrives as an `int` vector, while `isbn` (stored as a quoted string) correctly arrives as `chr`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3 · Reconcile types before comparing

Because the HTML parser returns everything as `character` while `fromJSON` preserves native JSON types, a direct `identical()` call would return `FALSE` due to the `pub_year` type mismatch — even though the values are logically the same. We coerce both frames to character to create a fair comparison.

```{r normalize}
# Coerce all columns to character in both frames so types align
df_html_norm <- as.data.frame(lapply(df_html, as.character),
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

df_json_norm <- as.data.frame(lapply(df_json, as.character),
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Guarantee identical column order (JSON key order may differ from HTML column order)
df_json_norm <- df_json_norm[, names(df_html_norm)]
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4 · Compare the two data frames

```{r compare}
are_identical <- identical(df_html_norm, df_json_norm)

cat("Are the two data frames identical?", are_identical, "\n")

# Detailed diff: show any cells that don't match
if (!are_identical) {
  mismatches <- which(df_html_norm != df_json_norm, arr.ind = TRUE)
  cat("Mismatches found at (row, col):\n")
  print(mismatches)
  cat("\nHTML values at mismatch positions:\n")
  print(df_html_norm[mismatches])
  cat("\nJSON values at mismatch positions:\n")
  print(df_json_norm[mismatches])
} else {
  cat("Both data frames contain exactly the same data.\n")
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5 · Side-by-side view

```{r side-by-side}
cat("--- HTML data frame ---\n")
print(df_html_norm)

cat("\n--- JSON data frame ---\n")
print(df_json_norm)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Summary

| Step | Key point |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| HTML → R | `rvest::html_table()` returns all values as `character`; trim whitespace |
| JSON → R | `jsonlite::fromJSON()` preserves native types (`int`, `chr`, etc.) |
| Type challenge | `pub_year` is `int` from JSON but `chr` from HTML; coerce before comparing |
| ISBN safety | Storing ISBN as a quoted string in JSON prevents 13-digit integer precision loss |
| Result | After normalization, `identical()` returns `TRUE` |
